prose: A yearlong Senate investigation led by Senators Warren, Van Hollen and Blumenthal argues that major tech firms are misleading the public about the true costs and benefits of AI data centers. The probe, shared first with TIME, covered seven developers: Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix, with staff requesting information and interviewing employees.

The findings, which largely match a year of news reporting, feed a broader congressional push to put guardrails around the power-intensive build-out. Warren has called for a national moratorium on new AI data centers until developers agree to cover the full costs, saying Congress must hold Big Tech accountable so companies pay their fair share.
highlights: Yearlong Senate probe of seven data-center developers
Warren, Van Hollen and Blumenthal led the investigation
Companies accused of misleading the public on costs and benefits
Warren wants a moratorium until developers cover full costs
Findings expected to feed broader guardrail legislation
